I'm planning Story 6.2 "Multi-Session Chat History & New Conversation" for a Flutter app (Cerne, Clean Architecture, flutter_bloc). Story 6.1 (send message + RAG streaming response) just shipped the chat feature's first vertical slice. I need a distilled investigation report (file paths + line numbers + short notes only, no long quotes) covering the following, so I can write an implementation spec without re-deriving it later:

**Acceptance criteria I'm implementing (verbatim from epics.md):**
- Given I have existing Chat Sessions, when I open the side menu, then they are listed and I can switch between them.
- Given I tap "Novo Chat" from the side menu, when a new session starts, then it opens empty with the composer focused and placeholder "Escreva uma mensagem..." — no invented greeting copy.
- Given I am offline, when I attempt to start a new Chat Session, then POST /chat/sessions is blocked, consistent with the offline composer lock on existing conversations.
- A returning (not new) session restores the last conversation's scroll position when opened.

**1. Current chat feature state (post-6.1), read these fully:**
- lib/features/chat/domain/entities/*.dart (ChatSession, ChatMessage, ChatStreamEvent shapes)
- lib/features/chat/domain/repositories/chat_repository.dart (existing abstract methods: listSessions, createSession, listMessages, sendMessage — exact signatures)
- lib/features/chat/data/repositories/chat_repository_impl.dart (Hive caching convention, how listSessions/createSession work, line numbers)
- lib/features/chat/data/datasources/chat_remote_data_source.dart (how listSessions/createSession call the backend — x-cerne-function names used)
- lib/features/chat/chat_injection.dart (DI registration, Hive box names)
- lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_state.dart and chat_cubit.dart (current sealed state shape, bootstrap logic — the "silently ensure one session exists, reuse most recent" logic and its exact line numbers, since 6.2 needs to replace/extend this with real session switching)
- lib/features/chat/presentation/screens/chat_screen.dart (header/drawer wiring, composer, scroll controller usage if any)

**2. Side menu / drawer:**
- lib/core/widgets/app_drawer.dart — full structure, how menu items are currently built, where a session list / "Novo Chat" entry would plausibly go, any existing scrollable list pattern inside it.

**3. Offline detection pattern already used in the codebase** (for reuse, not reinvention) — search for how the existing offline composer lock or offline banner (mentioned in epic context) is implemented, e.g. grep for "networkOffline", "offline", "NetworkInfo", "connectivity" across lib/features/chat and lib/core. Report exact file:line of whatever decides "are we offline" today.

**4. Backend contract for chat sessions** — read docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml around the chat.sessions paths (list/create) and report: exact x-cerne-function names, request/response schemas, whether there's any session-rename/delete endpoint, and whether list is paginated/cursor-based. Also check docs/input/backend/README.md for the path-to-function mapping table entries for chat sessions.

**5. Requirements doc** — docs/input/requirements.md: find the FR-24 section (multi-session chat history) and the endpoint-to-requirement mapping table rows for chat sessions endpoints, report line numbers and verbatim short excerpts only for FR-24's own text.

**6. Prototype extract** — docs/input/prototype/prototype-extract.md: search for side menu / "Novo Chat" / session list / drawer visual states, report line numbers and token names (colors/spacing) if specified; note if it's silent (in which case I'll need to decide per AGENTS.md policy).

**7. Existing test conventions for chat** — list test/features/chat/** files that exist, and note the DI-override/fake-repository pattern used in test/core/navigation/app_router_test.dart around lines 257-268 (mentioned in spec-6-1 as the pattern to mirror) — just confirm it's still there and report the exact current line range.

**8. Scroll-position precedent** — grep the codebase for any existing ScrollController persistence pattern (e.g. in entries list) that could be mirrored for "restore last scroll position."

Report everything as a compact structured list grouped by section number above, with file:line citations. Do not include code review opinions — just facts I need to write a spec. Keep total report under 700 lines of output.

- NEVER commit changes unless the user explicitly asks you to. It is VERY IMPORTANT to only commit when explicitly asked, otherwise the user will feel that you are being too proactive

1. Run the following bash commands in parallel, each using the Bash tool:
  - Run a git status command to see all untracked files. IMPORTANT: Never use the -uall flag as it can cause memory issues on large repos.
  - Run a git diff command to see both staged and unstaged changes that will be committed.
  - Run a git log command to see recent commit messages, so that you can follow this repository's commit message style.
2. Analyze all staged changes (both previously staged and newly added) and draft a commit message:
  - Summarize the nature of the changes (eg. new feature, enhancement to an existing feature, bug fix, refactoring, test, docs, etc.). Ensure the message accurately reflects the changes and their purpose (i.e. "add" means a wholly new feature, "update" means an enhancement to an existing feature, "fix" means a bug fix, etc.).
  - Do not commit files that likely contain secrets (.env, credentials.json, etc). Warn the user if they specifically request to commit those files
  - Draft a concise (1-2 sentences) commit message that focuses on the "why" rather than the "what"
  - Ensure it accurately reflects the changes and their purpose
3. Run the following commands in parallel:
   - Add relevant untracked files to the staging area.
   - Create the commit with a message, ending with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.
   - Run git status after the commit completes to verify success.

4. If the commit fails due to pre-commit hook: fix the issue and create a NEW commit

- NEVER run additional commands to read or explore code, besides git bash commands
- NEVER use the TodoWrite or Agent tools
- DO NOT push to the remote repository unless the user explicitly asks you to do so
- IMPORTANT: Never use git commands with the -i flag (like git rebase -i or git add -i) since they require interactive input which is not supported.
- IMPORTANT: Do not use --no-edit with git rebase commands, as the --no-edit flag is not a valid option for git rebase.
- If there are no changes to commit (i.e., no untracked files and no modifications), do not create an empty commit
- In order to ensure good formatting, ALWAYS pass the commit message via a HEREDOC, a la this example:
<example>
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
   Commit message here.
   EOF
   )"
</example>

# Creating pull requests
Use the gh command via the Bash tool for ALL GitHub-related tasks including working with issues, pull requests, checks, and releases. If given a Github URL use the gh command to get the information needed.

IMPORTANT: When the user asks you to create a pull request, follow these steps carefully:

1. Run the following bash commands in parallel using the Bash tool, in order to understand the current state of the branch since it diverged from the main branch:
   - Run a git status command to see all untracked files (never use -uall flag)
   - Run a git diff command to see both staged and unstaged changes that will be committed

2. Analyze all changes that will be included in the pull request, making sure to look at all relevant commits (NOT just the latest commit, but ALL commits that will be included in the pull request!!!), and draft a pull request title and summary:
   - Keep the PR title short (under 70 characters)
   - Use the description/body for details, not the title
3. Run the following commands in parallel:
   - Create new branch if needed
   - Push to remote with -u flag if needed
   - Create PR using gh pr create with the format below. Use a HEREDOC to pass the body to ensure correct formatting. End the body with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.
<example>
gh pr create --title "the pr title" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary
<1-3 bullet points>

## Test plan
[Bulleted markdown checklist of TODOs for testing the pull request...]
EOF
)"
</example>

tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem. You can access any file directly by using this tool.
Assume this tool is able to read all files on the machine. If the User provides a path to a file assume that path is valid. It is okay to read a file that does not exist; an error will be returned.

Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). 8	/// The chat feature's one port — `features/chat/presentation` depends on
9	/// this abstract class only, never `chat/data` (RNF06). Every method but
10	/// [sendMessage] returns `Future<Either<Failure, T>>` (RNF09); [sendMessage]
11	/// alone returns a `Stream` given the SSE nature of its response
12	/// (Boundaries).
13	abstract class ChatRepository {
14	  /// Calls `chat-sessions-list` (`ApiClient.get`, via
15	  /// `ChatRemoteDataSource`) — works offline via the `chat_sessions` Hive
16	  /// box (Code Map): on [Failure.networkOffline]/[Failure.networkTimeout],
17	  /// falls back to a full dump of that box, same "cache fallback"
18	  /// convention `EntriesRepositoryImpl.list()` already uses for its own
19	  /// first/fresh page. Every other [Failure] propagates as `Left`,
20	  /// unmapped (RNF09).
21	  Future<Either<Failure, List<ChatSession>>> listSessions();

24	  /// (Boundaries: "`chat-sessions-create` with no title") — blocked

26	  /// offline"), so unlike [listSessions] there is no cache fallback here:
27	  /// every [Failure], including [Failure.networkOffline], is returned as
28	  /// `Left`, unmapped. On success, persists the new session to the
29	  /// `chat_sessions` Hive box before returning `Right`, same
30	  /// "persist then return" ordering [listSessions] already uses.

34	  /// the one trailing path segment) — works offline via the

36	  /// [listSessions] already uses, filtered to [sessionId] and sorted by

41	  /// appended as the one trailing path segment) with `{content}` — the
42	  /// one streaming exception to this port's otherwise all-`Future` shape
43	  /// (Boundaries/RNF09: "every other method returns
44	  /// `Future<Either<Failure, T>>`"). No connectivity resolves immediately
45	  /// to a single `Left(Failure.networkOffline)` emission, never queued
46	  /// (Boundaries) — `ApiClient.postStream`'s own first awaited `Dio.post`

4	/// `ChatCubit`'s own sealed state — AD-12: "Chat's state is its own sealed
5	/// class, never forced into `Resource<T>`", because it isn't a single
6	/// fetch (the append-only [ChatReady.messages] list keeps growing one
7	/// token at a time while a response streams in, long after the initial
8	/// bootstrap fetch that produced it has already resolved).
9	sealed class ChatState {

11	}

14	/// session-bootstrap (list-or-create-one-session) + history fetch are
15	/// still in flight.

17	  const ChatBootstrapLoading();

20	/// I/O matrix: "Bootstrap failure" — `chat-sessions-list`/`create` (or the
21	/// history fetch right after) failed; the screen shows this generic error
22	/// state instead of spinning forever.
23	class ChatBootstrapError extends ChatState {
24	  const ChatBootstrapError(this.failure);
25	
26	  final Failure failure;
27	
28	  @override
29	  bool operator ==(Object other) =>
30	      identical(this, other) ||
31	      (other is ChatBootstrapError && other.failure == failure);
32	
33	  @override
34	  int get hashCode => failure.hashCode;
35	}

37	/// The composer is enabled, [messages] renders — [ChatUiMessage]'s own
38	/// [ChatUiMessage.status] drives each bubble's one of the 3 visible states
39	/// (streaming/failed/complete, RF04's Acceptance Criteria).
40	class ChatReady extends ChatState {
41	  const ChatReady({
42	    required this.sessionId,
43	    required this.messages,
44	    this.isSending = false,
45	  });
46	
47	  final String sessionId;
48	
49	  /// Append-only for the lifetime of this cubit (Code Map) — a message is
50	  /// ever only added to the end, or mutated in place by id (a streaming
51	  /// AI bubble's own `content`/`status`), never removed or reordered.
52	  final List<ChatUiMessage> messages;
53	
54	  /// Whether `ChatCubit.sendMessage`'s own send is actively in flight —
55	  /// the composer's one enable/disable signal (`_ChatComposer`). Kept as
56	  /// its own field rather than derived by scanning [messages] for a
57	  /// persisted `streaming` status: a message restored from history/cache
58	  /// can legitimately carry that status without a send being in flight
59	  /// (I/O matrix: mid-stream drop), which would otherwise permanently
60	  /// disable the composer.
61	  final bool isSending;
62	
63	  ChatReady copyWith({List<ChatUiMessage>? messages, bool? isSending}) =>
64	      ChatReady(
65	        sessionId: sessionId,
66	        messages: messages ?? this.messages,
67	        isSending: isSending ?? this.isSending,
68	      );

72	/// `ChatMessage` entity (Code Map) because a message in flight has no
73	/// server-assigned `seq`/`retryCount`/`createdAt` yet; [id] is a locally
74	/// generated, UI-only identifier (`ChatCubit._nextLocalId()`), never the
75	/// server's own message id (Design Notes: `message_created`'s id is the
76	/// *user* message's server id, unused by this story — see
77	/// `ChatStreamEvent`'s own doc).
78	class ChatUiMessage {
79	  const ChatUiMessage({
80	    required this.id,
81	    required this.role,
82	    required this.content,
83	    required this.status,
84	  });

86	  final String id;
87	  final ChatMessageRole role;
88	  final String content;
89	  final ChatMessageStatus status;
90	
91	  ChatUiMessage copyWith({String? content, ChatMessageStatus? status}) =>
92	      ChatUiMessage(
93	        id: id,
94	        role: role,
95	        content: content ?? this.content,
96	        status: status ?? this.status,
97	      );
98

100	  bool operator ==(Object other) =>

102	      (other is ChatUiMessage &&
103	          other.id == id &&
104	          other.role == role &&
105	          other.content == content &&
106	          other.status == status);
107	
108	  @override
109	  int get hashCode => Object.hash(id, role, content, status);
110	
111	  @override
112	  String toString() =>
113	      'ChatUiMessage(id: $id, role: $role, content: $content, '
114	      'status: $status)';

Doc comment (10-15) explicitly says session bootstrap logic lives in `ChatCubit.init()`, "kept in memory only" — i.e. no persisted "current session id" concept exists yet.
- `chat_message.dart:1-83` — `ChatMessageRole {user, assistant}` (2); `ChatMessageStatus {streaming, complete, failed}` (10); `ChatMessage` (19-82): `id, sessionId, role, content, seq, status, retryCount, createdAt`, has `copyWith({content, status})` (40-50).
- `chat_stream_event.dart:1-75` — sealed `ChatStreamEvent` (16-18); `ChatMessageCreatedEvent(userMessageId)` (26-42); `ChatTokenEvent(delta)` (47-61); `ChatDoneEvent` (64-75). `context` and `error` SSE events never become a `ChatStreamEvent` member (doc 1-10).

**Repository interface** (`lib/features/chat/domain/repositories/chat_repository.dart`)
- `listSessions()` → `Future<Either<Failure, List<ChatSession>>>` (line 21) — offline/timeout falls back to Hive cache.
- `createSession()` → `Future<Either<Failure, ChatSession>>` (line 31) — no title param; blocked offline, no cache fallback (doc 23-30).
- `listMessages(String sessionId)` → `Future<Either<Failure, List<ChatMessage>>>` (line 38).
- `sendMessage(String sessionId, String content)` → `Stream<Either<Failure, ChatStreamEvent>>` (lines 53-56) — the one streaming exception.
- **No `deleteSession`/`renameSession`/pagination param anywhere in this interface.** 6.2's "list sessions in side menu" has to call the existing `listSessions()` as-is (no cursor param threaded through yet — see §4).

**Repository impl** (`lib/features/chat/data/repositories/chat_repository_impl.dart`)
- Constructor takes `remoteDataSource`, `sessionsBox: Box<Map>`, `messagesBox: Box<Map>` (21-31).
- `listSessions()` (34-61): on success, `_sessionsBox.putAll({dto.id: dto.toJson()})` (49-51) then returns entities; on `NetworkOffline`/`NetworkTimeout` failure, calls `_cachedSessions()` (42-44); any other failure propagates unmapped.
- `createSession()` (64-86): on failure, **always** `left(failure)` — no offline fallback (67-70); on success, best-effort `_sessionsBox.put(dto.id, dto.toJson())` wrapped in try/catch that's intentionally swallowed (78-82) so a cache-write failure never masks an already-succeeded remote create.
- `listMessages(sessionId)` (88-113): same cache-write-then-return pattern; offline/timeout fallback is `_cachedMessages(sessionId)` (97-99).
- `sendMessage` (115-122): pure passthrough to data source, no Hive writes (Chat has no local write queue, per doc 120-122).
- `_cachedSessions()` (132-147): full Hive box dump, decodes each entry independently (one corrupt entry skipped, 139-141), sorted `updatedAt` desc (143-145) — this ordering is what lets `ChatCubit._bootstrap()`'s "most recent" pick stay correct even against cache.
- `_cachedMessages(sessionId)` (155-171): full box dump filtered by `sessionId`, sorted `seq` asc.

**Remote data source** (`lib/features/chat/data/datasources/chat_remote_data_source.dart`)

- `createSession()` (54-64) calls `_apiClient.post('chat-sessions-create', data: const {})` — explicitly sends no `title` even though the contract allows one (51-53 doc).
- `listMessages(sessionId)` (66-92) calls `_apiClient.get('chat-messages-list', pathParams: [sessionId])`.
- `sendMessage(sessionId, content)` (114-163) calls `_apiClient.postStream('chat-messages-send', pathParams: [sessionId], data: {'content': content})`; SSE parsing in `_parseEvent` (177-248).

**DI** (`lib/features/chat/chat_injection.dart`)

- `registerChatFeature()` (22-54): opens both boxes (23-24), registers them as named `Box<Map>` singletons (29-30), registers `ChatRemoteDataSource`/`ChatRepository` as lazy singletons (32-42), registers `ChatCubit` as a lazy singleton with `dispose: (cubit) => cubit.close()` (50-53) — doc (44-49) explains this is deliberate so a bootstrapped session survives navigating away and back within the same app run. **This lazySingleton-cubit shape is the thing 6.2 most needs to reconcile**: switching sessions / starting new ones must mutate this one long-lived cubit's state rather than re-resolving a fresh cubit per screen visit.

**Cubit state** (`lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_state.dart`)

  - 67: calls `_repository.listSessions()`.
  - 71-87: if `sessions.isEmpty` → `_repository.createSession()` (74); else re-sorts by `updatedAt` desc defensively (81-86) and picks `mostRecent.first` (86) — this is the "reuse the most recent" rule.
  - 92-113: on session resolved, calls `listMessages(session.id)` and emits `ChatReady(sessionId, messages)`.

- `sendMessage()` (139-206): guarded by `current is! ChatReady`, `_isSending` (148-150) — no offline check of its own; offline surfaces only as a stream `Left(Failure.networkOffline)` from the repository/ApiClient layer (see §3), not a pre-emptive UI lock.
- `close()` (291-299) cancels `_sendSubscription` and completes any pending `_sendCompleter`.

**Chat screen** (`lib/features/chat/presentation/screens/chat_screen.dart`)
